full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: Appellants are the heirs of plaintiff Afsaruddin. The appeal has been filed against the judgment dated May 13, 1997 in Civil Revision No. 2335 of 1992 passed by a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division making the Rule absolute and thereupon setting aside the judgment and decree dated July 6, 1992 of the 1st Court of Additional District Judge Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 185 of 1968 affirming the judgment and decree dated March 30, 1968 of the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka in Title Suit No. 22 of 1967 decreeing the suit. The suit was tiled seeking declaration of title, recovery of khas possession and for separate saham upon partition of the land in suit. 

 13. The defendant No.1 filed Miscellaneous Case seeking preemption in respect of the transfer made by Safatunnessa to the plaintiff but the said preemption case was dismissed being time barred. During the pendency of the preemption case defendant No.1 having had dispossessed the plaintiff, he (the plaintiff) filed the suit seeking declaration of title, khas possession and separate saham of 4 annas share from the land of CS plot No. 366 on partition of the land of the said plot. As stated hereinbefore that the defendant contested the suit taking two grounds. One was that plaintiff did not acquire any title by his purchase from Safatunnessa and that he at one stage of the suit filed an application under section 4 of the Partition Act to buyout the property purchased by the plaintiff on the contention that the land in suit is part of dwelling house of an undivided family. Before the lower appellate Court mainly it was argued that the property in suit being part of the dwelling house of an undivided family, the trial Court was in error in not allowing the prayer of the defendant No.1 to buy out the property in suit under section 4 of the Partition Act. The said contention of the appellant was not accepted by the appellate Court upon assigning reason. The High Court Division set aside the concurrent finding of the Court of facts that the property in suit is not part of the dwelling house of the undivided family on the view that the land in suit is contiguous to the homestead of defendant No.1 and that the defendant for convenient occupation of his house requires the hind in suit. It has already been mentioned that the defendant No.1 has not deposed in the case nor he has led any evidence to establish that the land in suit is part of the dwelling house of the undivided family to establish the fact as considered by the High Court Division while setting aside the finding of the Court of facts that the land in suit is not part of the dwelling house of an undivided family. From the pleading of the defendant and the evidence led from his side we do not find any foundation was laid by the defendant No.1 for availing the provision of section 4 of the Partition Act to buyout the land which the plaintiff purchased from Safatunnessa or, in other words, defendant has not established any case for buying out the land in suit under section 4 of the Partition Act. Defendant in a suit for partition to avail the provision of section 4 of the Partition Act is required to establish that the person seeking partition is stranger purchaser from the cosharer(s) of dwelling house of an undivided family. In the instant case, the defendant No.1 although filled an application under section 4 of the Partition Act stating that the suit property is the internal part of the homestead of this defendant No.1 and the plaintiff being a foreigner and outsider and has got no blood relation with this defendant and, as such, he cannot be allowed to remain or to live in the said suit property, with the members of this defendant on taking possession of the same". So, it is seen that defendant No.1 intended to buy the property purchased by the plaintiff on the ground that the property so purchased by the plaintiff "is the internal part" of the homestead or the defendant No.1. The defendant did not lead any evidence to substantiate the contention that. the suit property is "internal part" of his homestead. In that state of the matter the trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court concurrently held that property purchased by the plaintiff is not part of the dwelling house of an undivided family or, in other words, is not part of the homestead of the defendant No.1. Since the defendant No.1 did not establish any case to buy out the property in suit as per provision of section 4 of the Partition Act, the High Court Division was in serious error in holding that the land in suit is part of the dwelling house of the undivided family of the defendant No.1 and thereupon in setting aside the judgment of the lower appellate Court affirming the judgment of the trial Court which decreed the suit.
